title: ansible.builtin.win_ping: Default Windows temp directory resolution broken with 2.19
body:
### Summary

When we update from ansible-core 2.18.9 to 2.19.2 the win_ping module breaks because it does not seem to correctly resolve the Windows temporary directory (see logs) and therefore the payload cannot be copied to the remote server.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

pip

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> DEFAULT_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES(env: ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES) = True

Is there a reason why you have this enabled? This breaks pipelining and the reason why the temp dir is being created. While this should technically work it's more designed for debugging purposes and not something we fully test hence this error. I'll try and find the cause but you'll be better off just removing this setting and using the pipelined scenario as it is faster and simpler than having Ansible deal with a temp dir on every task.

comments.author: reporter

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Thanks for confirming, we did change the bootstrap wrapper used as the initial entrypoint for 2.19 and the subsequent scripts it executes for supporting WDAC as a new feature. In saying that the overall execution model hasn't really changed so I'm not sure why it is picking up this as a "trojan" but not before. Unfortunately this is more of a McAfee question to see why they think this is a trojan.

You could try using the [psrp](https://<redacted-host>/ansible/latest/collections/ansible/builtin/psrp_connection.html) connection plugin instead of `winrm` which still uses WSMan as the transport but has a different underlying API to provide the script to run. This *may* be enough to satisfy McAfee but I wouldn't be surprised if it did not. I'm sorry I don't have a better answer for you here but we don't have any insight into what McAfee is doing here and their detection rules so are at their mercy on what they are doing.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 how can I get my hands on the `exec_wrapper.ps1` file which is being blocked by the AV? I cannot find it on the remote system. I tried by simply creating it from https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.19/lib/ansible/executor/powershell/exec_wrapper.ps1 but the AV does not trigger in this case...

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
If you look at `AnsiballZ_win_ping.ps1` that was sent across in your example you'll see two segments separated by 4 null chars. The first is a JSON payload with the `exec_wrapper.ps1` and the second segment is the input data to `exec_wrapper`. All the scripts are located at https://github.com/ansible/ansible/tree/devel/lib/ansible/executor/powershell and you'll see that the initial `-EncodedCommand` value is essentially [bootstrap_wrapper.ps1](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/executor/powershell/bootstrap_wrapper.ps1) which in turn is used to run [exec_wrapper.ps1](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/executor/powershell/exec_wrapper.ps1). The reason why we have the `bootstrap_wrapper` first is for a two reasons:

+ Command line length limits won't allow us to use `-EncodedCommand` with `exec_wrapper.ps1`
+ When running in WDAC we need an initial stub to create the signed `exec_wrapper.ps1` and have PowerShell start it in Full Language Mode

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
OK, thanks, I managed to reproduce it manually by running `Get-Content .\AnsiballZ_win_ping.ps1 | .\bootstrap_wrapper.ps1`. The process then gets killed by the AV.

To get ahold of the 2.19 version of `AnsiballZ_win_ping.ps1` I had to copy the `ansible-local-xyz` temp directory from the source system while the command was still running. As soon as I use `ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1` (even with `ANSIBLE_SSH_PIPELINING=1`) I get the original error message because of the incomplete temp path. I think this should be fixed independently of the AV issue, right?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> I get the original error message because of the incomplete temp path. I think this should be fixed independently of the AV issue, right?

Ah sorry I forgot the put file operation failed when `ANSIBLE_KEEP_REMOTE_FILES=1` was set. That's related as copying the file also goes through `bootstrap_wrapper.ps1` with the same payload. Since that fails you have nothing in the temp file.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant3 looks like your issue is unrelated to the AV problem but something to do with the AWS SSM connection plugin. I'm not sure what has been broken but as that's not supported by Ansible they would have to investigate what is going wrong there and try and fix it up. Please redirect your issue to the [community.aws collection](https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.aws). Maybe the problem has stemmed from a change in Ansible and we need to fix it but it'll be up to the connection plugin author to try and figure out what may have gone wrong there.

Maybe the problem has stemmed from a change in Ansible and we need to fix it but it'll be up to the connection plugin author to try and figure out what may have gone wrong there.

For what it is worth, pinning ansible-core to version 2.18 with that same setup was successful with my tests with no other changes, but I am relatively new to setup of Ansible so the included aws collection plugin may have also been different with changing the core version.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: No worries, it's most likely due to the change in the execution runner in 2.19 but as I don't know how the AWS SSM connection plugin actually works it'll be up to them to figure out why the new payload isn't running properly. Happy for them to ping me on any issue they have once they've figured out the root cause or need further clarification on their side.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: We "fixed" this by adding the bootstrap wrapper file to the internal exclusion list. Apparently we will be moving to a different AV solution soon so the guys were reluctant to actually file this with the vendor (Trellix, formerly McAfee).
